products.name: Hour One
products.note: AI avatar video; virtual presenters; enterprise video; likeness consent; Israeli vendor

reading.body:
Hour One is an Israeli vendor selling AI avatar video and virtual presenters for enterprise use, with likeness consent noted as part of the product.

The company sits in video generation, a category where the output is a rendered person rather than text or code. That distinction matters for AI because avatar video is one of the few AI products whose cost is dominated by inference on continuous media, not by a single model call. Every minute of generated presenter footage is compute spent, and it is spent again for each new script.

The data covers very little beyond the product listing. There is no funding, no customer count, no model or infrastructure detail, and no power or data center information. Nothing here establishes where Hour One runs its inference or how much of it. The likeness consent note is the only governance signal present, and it is a product feature rather than a policy.

What the entry does not support is any claim about scale. A single product line and a website are not evidence of compute demand, and the reader should not read grid or power implications into a company profile this thin.
